summary: This Dockerfile creates a lightweight Alpine container that can clone private GitHub repositories using SSH. It sets up SSH client tools, configures GitHub's host key to prevent connection prompts, securely mounts an SSH private key at build time, tests the connection, and clones a private repository into the container.

explanations.3: This declares a build-time variable named KEY_NAME with a default value of 'id_rsa' (the standard SSH private key filename). You can override this when building with `--build-arg KEY_NAME=something_else`.
explanations.7: This installs essential tools we'll need: bash (shell), ca-certificates (for HTTPS), git (version control), and openssh-client (SSH tools). The --no-cache flag keeps the image smaller by not storing package manager cache.
explanations.10: This creates the .ssh directory with restrictive permissions (0700 means only the owner can read/write/execute) and pre-loads GitHub's public host key so SSH won't prompt us to verify it during cloning.
explanations.13: The --mount flag temporarily makes the SSH private key available during the build without storing it in the final image layers, keeping your secret safe. The key is mounted at the path /root/.ssh/${KEY_NAME} using the variable from line 3.
explanations.17: This tests the SSH connection to GitHub; the `|| true` means 'if this fails, that's okay, keep going anyway' so the build doesn't break if the test itself fails.
explanations.24: This keeps the container running indefinitely by having it continuously read from /dev/null (a special file that produces no output), preventing the container from exiting immediately after startup.
